essence: Five refusals charged — speak, see, hear, come, support — and scripture converts the charge into doctrine: the Lord is sense-free.

sections.SUMMARY: Five refusals charged — speak, see, hear, come, support — and scripture converts the charge into doctrine: the Lord is sense-free.
sections.EXPLANATION: No speaking to the wretched, no seeing, no hearing of the oft-made entreaty, no coming into the mind, no support amid the pit of transmigration's ocean — prāyeṇa, mostly, the single softening. Then the turn: sense-free by scripture's true declaration — devoid of speech, sight, hearing, feet and the like. The complaint is not answered; it is grounded. Denial upon denial becomes doctrine.
sections.BOUNDARY: Whether the turn to śruti is sincere resolution or ironic resignation is unresolved.
sections.RELATED: * Pancaślokī v.4 — the means that answer this reproach.

rasa.dominant: karuṇa (compassion-plea) shaded by adbhuta (wonder at doctrine)
rasa.justification: The sthāyibhāva is devotion (bhakti) in the mode of complaint (vijñapti); the vyabhicāri is despair (duḥkha), integrated by the turn to śruti's declaration of sense-freedom.
